answer: Each identity registers one seal from a public forge and files its plume pattern in a registry, locking a 60-credit bond. Auditors wander the forge log each epoch: two filings sharing one plume mark burn, one seal cannot carry two keys. Fees rise: first 35, kth 35+6(k-1); 1,000 fakes pay 3,032,000 +60,000 locked, against a 40,000 pool. A rented plume fails: its stamp binds its owner's key. Honest agents file once, pay 35, keep the bond.
